items.a_en: In research models, GHRH analogues bind the GHRH receptor on the growth hormone-producing cells of the pituitary, which triggers release of stored hormone. Ipamorelin binds the ghrelin receptor, a separate route that works alongside the GHRH signal. Growth hormone then acts on its own receptor around the body, and one of the main downstream results is IGF-1, produced largely in the liver. IGF-1 LR3 enters the pathway at that later stage and binds the IGF-1 receptor directly. None of them acts directly on muscle. These descriptions come from cell and animal research and establish no use outside the laboratory.

items.a_en: Each peptide is studied through a different mechanism, and none is fully understood. items.body_en: The Compounds in This Category Oxytocin A nine-amino-acid peptide hormone, Cys-Tyr-Ile-Gln-Asn-Cys-Pro-Leu-Gly-NH2, with a bridge between its two cysteines that closes part of it into a ring. Research uses it to study receptor signaling in tissue and animal models. PT-141 Also known as bremelanotide, a seven-amino-acid cyclic peptide related to melanotan II and to the natural hormone alpha-MSH. It binds the KISS1 receptor, also called GPR54, on neurons that release gonadotropin-releasing hormone. Research uses it to study how signals travel along the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. hCG Human chorionic gonadotropin is a glycoprotein hormone of 237 amino acids across two subunits, far larger than the other three compounds here. It binds the same receptor as luteinizing hormone. Because its activity is standardized biologically rather than by weight, it is supplied in international units.

items.q_en: What are Copper Peptides?
items.q_es: ¿Qué son los péptidos de cobre?
items.a_en: Copper peptides are short amino acid chains that hold a copper ion. The best known is GHK-Cu: glycine, histidine and lysine bound to copper. GHK was first identified in human plasma in 1973, and the material supplied for research today is made synthetically rather than extracted from any source. In laboratory models it has been studied for its effect on collagen and glycosaminoglycan synthesis, matrix remodelling, and gene expression linked to repair and antioxidant defence. Because the copper stays bound to the peptide, the complex is stable and unreactive in solution, which is one reason it is a convenient compound to work with at the bench. Supplied for laboratory research use only.

items.q_en: How Do Copper Peptides Work?
items.q_es: ¿Cómo funcionan los péptidos de cobre?
items.a_en: In study models, the peptide acts as a carrier: it holds copper in a stable, redox-silenced form and presents it to cells. Copper is a cofactor for enzymes involved in building and cross-linking connective tissue, including lysyl oxidase and superoxide dismutase. Research on GHK-Cu reports increased production of collagen, glycosaminoglycans and decorin in cultured fibroblasts, alongside changes in the genes that regulate how the matrix is broken down and rebuilt. One widely cited gene-expression analysis found the peptide shifted the activity of several thousand human genes in cultured cells. These findings come from in vitro and animal work.

items.body_en: How Are Collagen Peptides Used in Laboratory Research? Laboratory research on collagen peptides includes chemical characterization and experiments with defined peptide sequences. Researchers ask which fragments are present, how samples differ, and whether experimental conditions change the observations. These are questions about materials and laboratory models. They do not establish a personal application for a research vial or make different peptides interchangeable. Peptide Identification and Profiling Chromatography separates components of a collagen hydrolysate, while mass spectrometry helps characterize peptide masses and sequences. Researchers use these methods to describe a sample's peptide profile. A total protein figure alone cannot show which individual fragments are present or how they are distributed throughout the mixture. Experiments in Cell-Culture Models Collagen-derived peptides are also examined in cell-culture experiments, including studies using fibroblasts. Researchers measure endpoints such as cell numbers under defined experimental conditions. Background components in culture media can influence those measurements, so appropriate controls matter. These experiments describe observations in a laboratory model; they do not demonstrate what a supplier's vial will do in a person or establish a personal-use recommendation. Comparing Individual Peptide Sequences Some experiments focus on individual collagen-derived peptides, such as Pro-Hyp or Hyp-Gly, rather than an entire hydrolysate. Defined materials allow researchers to compare specific sequences and distinguish their observations from those obtained with a complex mixture. The exact peptide identity matters: sharing a collagen-related research topic does not make two compounds equivalent or establish that one can replace another experimentally. Batch and Analytical Method Comparisons Collagen hydrolysates can differ between batches, even when sold under the same general description. Analytical research compares peptide distributions and examines whether different measurement methods describe those samples consistently. This work helps define material specifications and identify variation that could affect experimental comparisons. Results remain tied to the tested samples, methods, and conditions; they are not a blanket certification of all collagen products.

items.a_en: Collagen peptides are short amino acid chains produced by breaking collagen down through hydrolysis. Collagen itself is a long triple-helix protein, and hydrolysis cuts it into fragments of varying length and sequence. A collagen hydrolysate is therefore a mixture rather than a single compound. Some research uses that mixture as supplied; other work uses a defined collagen-derived sequence such as prolyl-hydroxyproline (Pro-Hyp) or hydroxyprolyl-glycine (Hyp-Gly), which can be characterised precisely. The source collagen and the processing method both change what ends up in the material, which is why identity and batch documentation matter in this category. Supplied for laboratory research use only.
